subject.title: [Feature]: Built-in auto-update with configurable schedule, confirmation, and post-update notification

question: Should OpenClaw expand core `update.auto` into a first-class scheduled approval and notification workflow, and which parts belong in core versus Control UI, chat commands, or adjacent update-safety issues?
rationale: The request adds new config and unattended update semantics in a security-sensitive core workflow, so the approval model, channel delivery contract, persistence, and scope split need maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Keep As Core Workflow Tracker
options.body: Use this issue to design the remaining schedule, confirm or notify-only modes, channel delivery, and post-restart report behavior on the supervised update path.

options.title: Split To Narrow Follow-Ups
options.body: Keep only the engine requirements here and track UI discoverability, chat `/update`, rollback, plugin updates, and post-update hooks in their separate issues.

options.title: Decline Built-In Workflow
options.body: Keep only the current package auto-updater and document cron or agent workflows as operator-owned automation.

recommendation.title: Keep As Core Workflow Tracker
recommendation.body: Use this issue to design the remaining schedule, confirm or notify-only modes, channel delivery, and post-restart report behavior on the supervised update path.

likelyOwner.reason: The current updater feature history and latest maintainer-facing review context both route through steipete.
